item.title: Raspberry Pi Zero 2W: Driving AHT20 Sensor and Displaying Temperature & Humidity on OLED
item.description:
This article walks through how to drive an AHT20 temperature & humidity sensor with a Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W using Python, and display the readings on a 0.96-inch OLED screen (SSD1306/CH1116) with large fonts and a humidity progress bar. The project uses Python 3 with the smbus2 and Pillow libraries, with code generated with the help of Gemini AI.

Prerequisites

Item Description
Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W Running Raspberry Pi OS
AHT20 module Temperature & humidity sensor, I2C interface
0.96" OLED SSD1306 / CH1116 driver, I2C interface
Jumper wires Female-to-male, 4 pieces
Software Python 3, smbus2, Pillow, WenQuanYi Zen Hei font

Hardware Connection

Both the AHT20 and OLED use the I2C interface. Since the Raspberry Pi’s I2C bus supports multiple devices, simply connect them in parallel.

Module Pin Description Raspberry Pi Pin (Physical) Function
VCC Power (3.3V) Pin 1 3.3V Power
GND Ground Pin 9 Ground
SCL I2C Clock Pin 5 GPIO 3 (SCL)
SDA I2C Data Pin 3 GPIO 2 (SDA)

Software Setup

Enable I2C 

1

sudo raspi-config

Navigate to Interface Options → I2C → Yes, save and reboot.

Install Chinese Font

sudo apt update
sudo apt install fonts-wqy-zenhei

source myenv/bin/activate

# Install smbus2 (I2C driver) and Pillow (image processing)
pip3 install -i https://pypi.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/simple smbus2 Pillow

Usage

  1. Make sure I2C is enabled (see Software Setup)
  2. Activate the virtual environment: source myenv/bin/activate
  3. Run the script: python3 oled_aht20.py
  4. The OLED will refresh temperature and humidity readings every 2 seconds

import time
import os
from smbus2 import SMBus
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont

# --- Configuration ---
I2C_BUS = 1
AHT20_ADDR = 0x38
OLED_ADDR = 0x3C


# --- Font Loading ---
def get_font(size):
    """Try multiple common paths to find a Chinese font"""
    font_paths = [
        "simhei.ttf",
        "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/wqy/wqy-zenhei.ttc",
        "/usr/share/fonts/opentype/noto/NotoSansCJK-Regular.ttc"
    ]
    for path in font_paths:
        if os.path.exists(path):
            return ImageFont.truetype(path, size)

    print(f"Warning: Chinese font not found, using default (size: {size})")
    return ImageFont.load_default()


# --- OLED Driver ---
def oled_command(bus, cmd):
    bus.write_byte_data(OLED_ADDR, 0x00, cmd)


def oled_init(bus):
    """Initialize OLED with charge pump and page addressing mode"""
    cmds = [0xAE, 0xD5, 0x80, 0xA8, 0x3F, 0xD3, 0x00, 0x40, 0x8D, 0x14,
            0x20, 0x02, 0xA1, 0xC8, 0xDA, 0x12, 0x81, 0xCF, 0xD9, 0xF1,
            0xDB, 0x40, 0xA4, 0xA6, 0xAF]
    for c in cmds:
        oled_command(bus, c)


def oled_display(bus, image):
    """Push a PIL Image to the OLED"""
    img = image.convert("1")
    pix = img.load()
    for page in range(8):
        oled_command(bus, 0xB0 + page)
        oled_command(bus, 0x00)
        oled_command(bus, 0x10)
        page_data = []
        for x in range(128):
            byte = 0
            for bit in range(8):
                if pix[x, page * 8 + bit]:
                    byte |= (1 << bit)
            page_data.append(byte)
        for i in range(0, 128, 32):
            bus.write_i2c_block_data(OLED_ADDR, 0x40, page_data[i:i + 32])


# --- AHT20 Sensor ---
def read_aht20(bus):
    """Read AHT20, returns (temperature in °C, humidity in %)"""
    bus.write_i2c_block_data(AHT20_ADDR, 0xAC, [0x33, 0x00])
    time.sleep(0.08)
    data = bus.read_i2c_block_data(AHT20_ADDR, 0x71, 7)
    h_raw = ((data[1] << 12) | (data[2] << 4) | (data[3] >> 4))
    t_raw = ((data[3] & 0x0F) << 16) | (data[4] << 8) | data[5]
    return (t_raw / 1048576 * 200 - 50), (h_raw / 1048576 * 100)


# --- Main Program ---
def main():
    bus = SMBus(I2C_BUS)
    oled_init(bus)

    # Load three font sizes
    f_huge = get_font(30)   # Temperature digits
    f_mid = get_font(16)    # Labels
    f_small = get_font(12)  # Unit symbols

    while True:
        try:
            temp, humi = read_aht20(bus)
            img = Image.new("1", (128, 64))
            draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img)

            # --- Temperature display ---
            t_str = f"{temp:.1f}"
            draw.text((5, -2), t_str, font=f_huge, fill=255)
            t_w = draw.textlength(t_str, font=f_huge)
            draw.text((5 + t_w + 2, 12), "°C", font=f_mid, fill=255)

            # --- Separator line ---
            draw.line((0, 31, 128, 31), fill=255)

            # --- Humidity display ---
            draw.text((5, 35), f"Humidity:", font=f_mid, fill=255)
            draw.text((50, 35), f"{humi:.1f}%", font=f_mid, fill=255)

            # --- Humidity progress bar ---
            draw.rectangle((5, 54, 122, 60), outline=255, fill=0)
            bar_w = int(humi / 100 * 115)
            draw.rectangle((7, 56, 7 + bar_w, 58), outline=255, fill=255)

            oled_display(bus, img)
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error: {e}")

        time.sleep(2)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

item.title: Using Raspberry Pi Zero 2W to Drive a Screen and Play Videos
item.description:
This article demonstrates how to drive a 1.8-inch TFT screen (ST7735S chip) using Python to play MP4 videos. The code was generated with the help of Gemini AI.

Prerequisites

Item Description
Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W Running Raspberry Pi OS
1.8" TFT LCD ST7735S chip, SPI interface
Jumper wires Female-to-male, 8 pieces
Software Python 3, luma.lcd, opencv-python, Pillow

Hardware Connection

Based on the LCD pin definitions (GND, VCC, SCL, SDA, RES, DC, CS, BL), connect as follows:

LCD Pin Description Raspberry Pi Pin (Physical) Function
GND Ground Pin 6 / 9 / 14 etc. GND
VCC Power (3.3V) Pin 1 or Pin 17 3.3V Power
SCL SPI Clock (CLK) Pin 23 GPIO 11 (SPI0_SCLK)
SDA SPI Data (MOSI) Pin 19 GPIO 10 (SPI0_MOSI)
RES Reset Pin 22 GPIO 25 (customizable)
DC Data/Command Select Pin 18 GPIO 24 (customizable)
CS Chip Select Pin 24 GPIO 8 (SPI0_CE0)
BL Backlight Control Pin 12 or Pin 1 GPIO 18 or 3.3V

Check pin definitions: pinout

Software Setup

Enable SPI 

1

sudo raspi-config

Navigate to Interface Options → SPI → Yes, save and reboot.

Install Dependencies 

1

pip3 install luma.lcd opencv-python Pillow

Usage

  1. Make sure SPI is enabled (see Software Setup)
  2. Place the MP4 video file in the same directory as the script
  3. Run: python3 play_video.py video_name.mp4

import cv2
import time
from luma.lcd.device import st7735
from luma.core.interface.serial import spi
from PIL import Image

# --- Hardware initialization (60MHz) ---
serial = spi(port=0, device=0, gpio_DC=24, gpio_RST=25, baudrate=60000000)
try:
    device = st7735(serial, width=160, height=128, rotate=0, bgr=False,
                    h_offset=1, v_offset=2)
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Initialization failed: {e}")
    exit(1)


def play_video_fast(video_path):
    cap = cv2.VideoCapture(video_path)
    if not cap.isOpened():
        print(f"Cannot open video: {video_path}")
        return

    # Get video frame rate
    fps = cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FPS)
    frame_duration = 1.0 / fps

    print(f"Original FPS: {fps}, Target resolution: {device.width}x{device.height}")

    start_time = time.time()
    frame_count = 0

    try:
        while cap.isOpened():
            ret, frame = cap.read()
            if not ret:
                break

            frame_count += 1

            # --- Dynamic frame skipping ---
            # Calculate which frame should be displayed now; skip any that fall behind
            elapsed = time.time() - start_time
            expected_frame = int(elapsed / frame_duration)

            if frame_count < expected_frame:
                continue

            # --- Image processing ---
            # 1. Resize to screen dimensions (resize before color conversion saves CPU)
            small_frame = cv2.resize(frame, (device.width, device.height),
                                     interpolation=cv2.INTER_NEAREST)

            # 2. Color conversion (BGR → RGB)
            rgb_frame = cv2.cvtColor(small_frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)

            # 3. Convert to PIL image and display
            img = Image.fromarray(rgb_frame)
            device.display(img)

    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print("Playback stopped")
    finally:
        cap.release()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import sys
    video = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "video.mp4"
    play_video_fast(video)
